newsitem.title: FRANCE: French sugar beets doing well on favourable weather.
newsitem.headline: French sugar beets doing well on favourable weather.

text.p: Prospects for the 1997/98 sugar beet harvest in France are very good with the crop getting just the right mix of moisture and sunshine, planters said on Wednesday.
Barring a weather accident in the two months before the harvest starts in October, beet and sugar yields should be well above last year, they said.

"Everything is fine. Showers are bringing moisture and there is sunshine. The beets are getting a steady amount of moisture and they are disease-free," an analyst for the national sugar beet planters federation (CGB) told Reuters.
A combination of sunshine and showers boosted leaf and root growth and crop development remains ahead of last year.
Asked about prospects for 1997/98 yields, the analyst predicted that the average beet yield could rise to over 60 tonnes per hectare from 56 tonnes achieved last year.
He repeated previous forecasts that the crop would exceed last year's sugar yield of 10 tonnes per hectare.
"We can assume this (10 tonnes) is now assured," he said.
On August 4 beet planters will conduct their first beet test that measures sugar weight, number of beets per hectare and sugar content.
The test runs in parallel with that carried out by the sugar manufacturers' association (SNFS).
France produced 4.226 million tonnes of beet sugar last year.
